title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.

steps.action: Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
Make sure all slices together equal 100.
Focus only on your true share.
Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Repair”; release extra blame.
“Find Your Slice” keeps blame in proportion.
I can use “Share The Slices” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.

steps.action: Picture two arrows.
One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
Select by direction, not by mental volume.

win: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
supports: Exhale after “Select Direction”; keep the compass.
I can use “Make Room” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Picture → Make Room → Name Likely → Select Direction
safety:
PAUSE
Choose safety over values exercises during acute crisis or impairment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

steps.action: Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

win: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Next”; release the score.
I can use “Read Protest” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pretend closure for urgent, coercive, unsafe, or irreversible choices.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
goal: When the path is missing, choose the way of walking.

steps.action: Ask: ‘What quality do I want this the action you can take now to carry?’ Pick one—honesty, courage, care, fairness, patience.
Define how that quality would look in a single visible movement today.
Let certainty remain absent while the compass gives direction.

win: ✓ Certainty stayed missing. Direction did not.
supports: Exhale after “Let Certainty”; keep the compass.
I can use “Look Single” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Ask Quality → Look Single → Let Certainty
safety:
PAUSE
Recheck practical facts when uncertainty involves significant legal, financial, or health risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD
goal: Some solutions survive only because their costs stay hidden.

steps.action: Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, extra certainty, overworking.
Beside each, picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.

win: ✓ One hidden control-cost just lost today’s payment.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Experiment”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Picture Short” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Use Control → Picture Short → Focus On Costs → Choose Experiment
safety:
PAUSE
Do not remove prescribed treatment or essential safety behaviour without professional advice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MORE THAN THIS STATE
goal: A single moment cannot legally seize your whole identity.

steps.action: Name three roles you carry, two qualities others have witnessed, and one state present today.
Imagine a large Focus on around all six.
Place the current painful content inside, not across, the boundary.
Ask which part of the larger system should lead the one simple action.

win: ✓ This state stayed one part of me, not the whole system.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Part”; release extra load.
I can use “Imagine Large” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Carry Qualities → Imagine Large → Place Painful → Ask Part
safety:
PAUSE
Use simple grounding instead if expansion feels abstract or dissociative.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE THIRD VOICE
goal: Emotion and logic are witnesses; wisdom gives the final answer.

steps.action: Complete three lines.
FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
Read only the third line before acting.

win: ✓ Emotion stayed real; the verdict became negotiable.
supports: Exhale after “Use Wisdom”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Name Feeling” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Open Voices → Name Feeling → Name Facts → Build Wisdom → Use Wisdom
safety:
PAUSE
Delay major action if either witness is too impaired to give usable information.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT JOB IS THIS FEELING DOING?
goal: An emotion is a messenger with several departments.

steps.action: Ask three questions separately: What change is it signalling?
What action is it preparing?
What is it communicating to others?
Keep answers concrete.
Use the information. Keep the behaviour under your supervision.

win: ✓ The feeling delivered its message without taking over behaviour.
supports: Exhale after “Use the Message”; let feeling settle.
“Ask Separately” to “Use the Message”: what loosened?
I can use “Prepare Action” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Ask Separately → Prepare Action → Communicating → Keep Concrete → Use the Message
safety:
PAUSE
Do not overanalyse when regulation or immediate safety comes first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHECK THE BIOLOGICAL VOLUME KNOBS
goal: Sometimes the mind is loud because the body is missing basic care.

steps.action: Review five amplifiers: illness or pain; missed food or hydration; substances or withdrawal; sleep debt; movement deficit or excess.
Spot the strongest correctable factor.
Make one health-supporting adjustment before treating the entire reaction as psychological truth.

win: ✓ The body got basic care before the mind got blamed.
supports: Gently exhale after “Make Health”; no forcing.
I can use “Identify Strongest” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Review → Identify Strongest → Make Health
safety:
PAUSE
Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, medication concerns, or dangerous withdrawal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PRELIVE THE HARD MOMENT
goal: Rehearsal can give the future a familiar exit.

steps.action: Picture the trigger beginning.
Insert the exact skill you will use, the obstacle most likely to interrupt it, and your recovery if that obstacle wins once.
Continue the scene through a realistic ending—not a perfect one.
Then place one physical reminder where the event starts.

win: ✓ The target became human-sized.
supports: Exhale after “Place Physical”; release the score.
I can use “Use Obstacle” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Picture → Use Obstacle → Continue Scene → Place Physical
safety:
PAUSE
Keep imagery brief if anticipation escalates instead of preparing you.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FEELING OR FIXING?
goal: Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.

steps.action: After body alarm drops, define the obstacle without emotional adjectives.
Ask if one specific action could change it.
If yes, choose and schedule that action.
If no, return to acceptance or support.
Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key.

win: ✓ Soothing stopped where a real key was needed. The next move became practical.
supports: Gently exhale after “Stop Soothing”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Ask Whether” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Drop Define → Ask Whether → Choose Action → Return Acceptance → Stop Soothing
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid problem-solving while too activated to assess consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FINISH THE LOOK
goal: Defence narrows the world; orientation in the present reopens it.

steps.action: Let your eyes move before your head.
Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
End by selecting where attention belongs now.

win: ✓ Now is back in the foreground.
supports: Gently exhale after “Place Attention”; no forcing.
I can use “Scan Left” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Let Eyes → Scan Left → Name Cues → Allow Neck → Place Attention
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid head movement with injury, dizziness, or driving.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE DROP, NOT THE OCEAN
goal: One drop can teach what the ocean would drown.

steps.action: Choose the tiniest fragment of the difficult material: one edge, colour, word, or body sensation.
Contact it briefly, then return fully to a stabilising cue.
Hold the dose that allowed recovery.
Next practice uses the same or less—not an ambitious leap.

win: ✓ I touched one drop of the feeling without turning it into the ocean.
supports: Gently exhale after “Use Less”; no forcing.
I can use “Return Fully” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Choose Tiniest → Return Fully → Find Dose → Use Less
safety:
PAUSE
Seek trained support when even minimal contact overwhelms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
goal: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.

steps.action: Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
Add only that ingredient.

win: ✓ One useful ingredient found; the rest can stay off the recipe.
supports: Exhale after “Add Ingredient”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Describe Boundaries” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Locate Bodily → Describe Boundaries → Ask Memory → Add Ingredient
safety:
PAUSE
Choose an external anchor if internal tracking feels inaccessible or unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAP YOUR OPERATING WINDOW
goal: Know the edges before you cross them.

steps.action: Picture three operating zones: TOO HIGH, WORKABLE, TOO LOW.
Add your earliest personal signs in body, speech, attention, and behaviour.
Beside each outer zone, picture the fastest safe route toward the middle.
Place the imagined path where others can help recognise it.

win: ✓ Past and present are separate rooms again.
supports: Gently exhale after “Place Others”; orient to now.
I can use “Add Earliest” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Imagine Zones → Add Earliest → Picture Fastest → Place Others
safety:
PAUSE
Use professional guidance when shutdown, mania, trauma, or severe loss of steadiness is involved.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
goal: Remove the manager from respiration.

steps.action: Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
Between breaths, let the body choose again.
Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

win: ✓ The thought moved from identity to object.
supports: Exhale after “Witness Motion”; watch the thought.
I can use “Leave Breath Alone” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion
safety:
PAUSE
Use outward sensory contact if breath attention increases panic or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RHYTHM BEFORE DEPTH
goal: Rhythm first. Depth can follow.

steps.action: Choose a slow, comfortable pace in which inhale and exhale feel smooth.
Use a quiet timer or gentle movement as metronome, never forcing lung volume.
Continue long enough to find a repeatable rhythm, then remove the metronome and keep one easy cycle.

win: ✓ Motion replaced the waiting game.
supports: Exhale after “Continue Long”; then keep moving.
I can use “Use Quiet” before motivation.
formula_flow: Choose Slow → Use Quiet → Continue Long
safety:
PAUSE
Abandon pacing if it feels restrictive or medically unsuitable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE EVEN BRIDGE
goal: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.

steps.action: Pick a count that requires no effort.
Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.

win: ✓ Noise separated into something the mind can hold.
supports: Exhale after “Complete Few”; then keep moving.
I can use “Count Exhale” before motivation.
formula_flow: Pick Requires → Count Exhale → Imagine Pair → Complete Few
safety:
PAUSE
Return to spontaneous breathing if equality creates pressure.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BREATHE THE GESTURE
goal: Give respiration a visible partner.

steps.action: Take one slow movement with two directions—arms open and close, rise and lower, reach and return.
Pair the expansive direction with inhale and the returning direction with exhale.
Let movement size follow comfort, then complete one cycle without conscious pairing.

win: ✓ The task lost enough weight to begin.
supports: Exhale after “Let Movement”; then keep moving.
I can use “Return Direction” before motivation.
formula_flow: Choose Slow → Return Direction → Let Movement
safety:
PAUSE
Modify for pain, balance issues, fatigue, or mobility limits.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
goal: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

steps.action: Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.

win: ✓ The social scoreboard stopped being the whole room.
supports: Exhale after “Hold Conclusions”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Ask Claims” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Picture Appears → Ask Claims → Hold Conclusions
safety:
PAUSE
Discontinue if sleep-related inquiry worsens insomnia or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES
goal: Stability is trained before the verdict arrives.

steps.action: Imagine the action succeeding.
State what that value asks of you next.
Imagine it failing.
State how the same value responds there.
Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.

win: ✓ Meaning found a next move without denying the pain.
supports: Exhale after “Let Outcome”; keep both sides.
I can use “State Governing” before concluding.
formula_flow: Imagine Action → State Governing → Imagine Failing → State Value → Let Outcome
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use equanimity to ignore grief, accountability, or material consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE
goal: Extremes can impersonate discipline.

steps.action: Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
Use the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.

win: ✓ The ignored side regained a vote.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Smallest”; keep both sides.
I can use “Find Area” before concluding.
formula_flow: Rest Review → Find Area → Set Middle → Choose Smallest
safety:
PAUSE
Medical and nutritional needs should override generic moderation advice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
goal: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.

steps.action: Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
Do not organise while emptying.
When the mind offers silence, sort entries into do, schedule, delegate, reference, or delete.
Choose only the first physical action.

win: ✓ Mental countertop cleared. One physical move remains.
supports: One exhale after “Choose Physical”; redirect attention.
I can use “Empty First” amid noise.
formula_flow: Question Promise → Empty First → Sort Entries → Choose Physical
safety:
PAUSE
Protect confidential material and avoid endless Name refinement.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE REQUEST SPINE
goal: Clear and firmness needs structure when emotion bends the message.

steps.action: Say the visible situation.
Express its impact.
Assert the exact request or no.
Reinforce why cooperation helps.
Picture one sentence for each part, then deliver the leanest version.

win: ✓ The request kept its backbone and lost the extra weight.
supports: Exhale after “Picture Sentence”; release extra load.
I can use “Express Impact” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Describe Situation → Express Impact → Assert Request → Reinforce Cooperation → Picture Sentence
safety:
PAUSE
Use support or distance when direct assertion could provoke danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING
goal: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.

steps.action: Picture three separate statements: their behaviour; what effect it had; what you do not know about intention.
Base your next boundary on behaviour and impact.
Leave motive open until reliable evidence or direct communication updates it.

win: ✓ The need to know shrank below the need to live the next minute.
supports: Exhale after “Leave Motive”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Base” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Separate Unknown → Base → Leave Motive
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use uncertainty about motive to postpone urgent protection.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED
goal: Other minds are opaque until they speak and behave.

steps.action: Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.
Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence.
Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active.

win: ✓ Curiosity stayed open without pretending I could read another mind.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Behaviour”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Replace Possibilities” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Catch Sentence → Replace Possibilities → Possibility → Choose Behaviour
safety:
PAUSE
Trust documented patterns when direct questioning is unsafe or repeatedly manipulated.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
goal: Two competing experiences can become one pattern.

steps.action: Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
Decide only after the braid is complete.

win: ✓ Two competing signals became one braid I could actually read.
supports: One exhale after “Decide After”; redirect attention.
I can use “Alternate B” amid noise.
formula_flow: Choose Signals → Alternate B → Hold Time → Decide After
safety:
PAUSE
Do not braid a safety alarm with pressure to ignore it.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.

steps.action: Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

win: ✓ I matched the pressure, brought it back to zero, and checked what remained.
supports: Exhale after “Reach Zero”; mark the pause.
I can use “Match Force” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Press Equal → Match Force → Step Down → Reach Zero
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this with pain, hand or joint injury, numbness, breath holding, or any unsafe physical symptom.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
goal: Direct data can update the relationship model.

steps.action: Picture the assumption driving your reaction.
Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong.
Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model.

win: ✓ Fear finally answered the question it had been answering for me.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Suitable”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Question Whose” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Assumption → Question Whose → Ask Suitable
safety:
PAUSE
Skip direct questioning when manipulation, violence, or coercion makes it unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TRANSLATE ACROSS SENSES
goal: A vague state can become workable in another medium.

steps.action: Represent tension as a texture, a sound as a shape, or an emotion as colour and movement.
Make the translation concrete enough to Imagine or gesture.
Alter one property in the new medium and observe if the first state changes.

win: ✓ I translated the state into another sense and changed one property there.
supports: One exhale after “Observe Whether”; redirect attention.
I can use “Make Translation” amid noise.
formula_flow: Represent → Make Translation → Observe Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if cross-sensory imagery becomes confusing or perceptually disturbing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COUNT EVERY OPEN LOOP
goal: Invisible commitments keep using memory until named.

steps.action: Name every unresolved promise, question, task, decision, and waiting item without solving any.
Use one line each.
When nothing else appears for thirty seconds, imagine a boundary around the inventory and choose a separate processing time.

win: ✓ Then lost some of its grip on now.
supports: Exhale after “Imagine Boundary”; mark the pause.
I can use “Use Line” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Question Task → Use Line → Imagine Boundary
safety:
PAUSE
End the capture if list-making increases overwhelm without containment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES
goal: Ideas, duties, fears, and memories should not share one queue.

steps.action: Catch each mental item, then route it into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION.
Give each category its own processing rule.
Prioritise only after sorting, so emotional intensity does not determine inbox order.

win: ✓ The mind got separate queues instead of one emergency pile.
supports: Exhale after “Don't Determine”; mark the pause.
I can use “Give Category” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Question Capture → Give Category → Don't Determine
safety:
PAUSE
Add categories sparingly; excessive sorting can become avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WANT NOW / PROTECT LATER
goal: Desire and value need separate lanes.

steps.action: Picture what the present urge wants, then what future life is worth protecting.
Name the cost each imposes on the other.
Choose one action that acknowledges desire while keeping the valued asset intact.

win: ✓ Desire stayed acknowledged while the future asset stayed protected.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Action”; mark the pause.
I can use “Name Cost” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Picture Urge → Name Cost → Choose Action
safety:
PAUSE
Seek support when cravings threaten safety, sobriety, or financial control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PREVIEW THE AFTER
goal: Delayed reward is undercounted because the mind cannot feel it yet.

steps.action: Picture a ten-second scene immediately after completion: what is lighter, available, learned, protected, or enjoyed?
Include a sensory marker plus one practical consequence.
Begin the task while that specific after-state remains accessible.

win: ✓ Delay lost its claim on the next minute.
supports: One exhale after “State Accessible”; redirect attention.
I can use “Include Sensory” amid noise.
formula_flow: Protect Enjoyed → Include Sensory → State Accessible
safety:
PAUSE
Do not fabricate benefits that the action is unlikely to deliver.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BORING DOSE
goal: Low stimulation can be trained in measured practice round.

steps.action: Set up a boring task that is safe and preselect a short interval.
Remove entertainment but keep necessary tools.
Stay with boredom’s body sensations until the timer ends, then stop even if you could continue.
Increase future doses slowly.

win: ✓ I took a measured dose of boring and proved I could stay.
supports: Gently exhale after “Raise the Dose”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Remove Entertainment” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Choose Safe → Remove Entertainment → Stay Boredom → Raise the Dose
safety:
PAUSE
Adapt for attention disorders and never use boredom as punishment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BUILD MEANING ON FIVE LEGS
goal: One collapsed source should not fell the whole table.

steps.action: Rate meaning currently available through relationship, contribution, growth, experience, and transcendence.
Choose the weakest repairable leg and one small action that strengthens it.
Keep the strongest leg from carrying everything.

win: ✓ The present gained evidence the memory cannot overwrite.
supports: Gently exhale after “Keep Strongest”; orient to now.
I can use “Choose Weakest” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Rate Meaning → Choose Weakest → Keep Strongest
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pluralism to avoid repairing a central loss that needs care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT PREPARATION DID WORRY ACTUALLY PRODUCE?
goal: Imagined work should show a deliverable.

steps.action: Name every concrete preparation created by the worry.
Separate useful actions from repeated simulation.
If the list contains a real gap, prepare once.
If no gap remains, label further worry UNPAID OVERTIME.

win: ✓ Worry produced no new deliverable. Overtime cancelled.
supports: Gently exhale after “Remain Name”; orient to now.
I can use “Separate Useful” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Create Worry → Separate Useful → Prepare Name → Remain Name
safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss new information simply because worry has repeated.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MARK THE QUALITY DROP
goal: Analysis needs an exit before fatigue corrupts it.

steps.action: Define your personal decline signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower comprehension, repeated searches, no new distinctions.
When two appear, stop and hold the last reliable conclusion.
Recovery precedes any reopening.

win: ✓ I caught the moment thinking quality dropped and exited before fatigue took over.
supports: Exhale after “Start Recovery”; keep both sides.
I can use “Stop Last” before concluding.
formula_flow: Repeat No → Stop Last → Start Recovery
safety:
PAUSE
Continue only when delay creates greater risk than reduced quality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.

steps.action: Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.

win: ✓ The worry cycle lost its automatic restart.
supports: Gently exhale after “Keep Fact”; orient to now.
I can use “Halve Speed” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Recall Exchange → Halve Speed → Shift → Keep Fact
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if replay raises distress, becomes compulsive, or concerns abuse or danger that requires support and protection.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THOUGHTS WEIGHTED VOTES
goal: Mental statements should not all receive one ballot.

steps.action: For each influential thought, score evidence, relevant expertise, recency, and decision relevance.
Multiply nothing; simply rank.
Let the highest-quality thought advise the action while lower-ranked voices remain recorded but nonbinding.

win: ✓ The loudest thought lost the automatic deciding vote.
supports: Gently exhale after “Let Highest”; orient to now.
I can use “Multiply” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Score Evidence → Multiply → Let Highest
safety:
PAUSE
Do not confuse confidence, status, or repetition with expertise.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: AUCTION THE NEXT ATTENTION BLOCK
goal: Limited attention needs a clear way to choose.

steps.action: Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value.
Total the four ratings.
Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires.
Re-auction with updated evidence.

win: ✓ My next attention block went to the highest-value bidder.
supports: Exhale after “Update Evidence”; slow the clock.
formula_flow: Let Active → Total → Protect Block → Update Evidence
safety:
PAUSE
Emergency signals may override the auction immediately.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
goal: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.

steps.action: Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

win: ✓ Five icons exposed the repeat—and one place to exit.
supports: Exhale after “Choose An Exit”; end the lap.
If it flares, choose “Spot The Return”.
“Spot The Return” proves loops can stop.
I can use “Imagine Five Signs” without another lap.
formula_flow: No Sentences → Imagine Five Signs → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit
safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
goal: Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.

steps.action: Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
Arrange them as they feel now.
Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration.
Name the real-life action equivalent to that move.

win: ✓ The abstract problem moved on the table—and revealed a real-world move.
supports: Gently exhale after “Name Real”; orient to now.
I can use “Feel Arrange” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Use Small → Feel Arrange → Move Object → Name Real
safety:
PAUSE
Do not treat symbolic placement as factual evidence about other people.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
goal: The future gets easier when it already feels familiar.

steps.action: Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.

win: ✓ The future felt remembered enough for the first movement to become obvious.
supports: One exhale after “Look Backward”; redirect attention.
I can use “Include Time” amid noise.
formula_flow: Create Memory → Include Time → Look Backward
safety:
PAUSE
Keep future scenes realistic rather than using fantasy as avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.

steps.action: Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?
What do you fear will happen?
What would make one step acceptable?
Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.

win: ✓ Resistance revealed the need it was trying to protect.
supports: Gently exhale after “Picture Negotiate”; orient to now.
I can use “Ask Fear” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Give Obstacle → Ask Fear → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
safety:
PAUSE
Do not personify intrusive voices or experiences if that worsens symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
goal: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.

steps.action: Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
Try that small change once.

win: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
supports: Exhale after “Test It”; mark the pause.
“Find the Lever” proves choice interrupted habit.
“Imagine The Parts” versus “Test It”: what eased?
I can use “See The Links” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Imagine The Parts → See The Links → Find the Lever → Test It
safety:
PAUSE
Keep the mental picture simple. Stop if you begin analysing without taking action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
goal: Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.

steps.action: Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.
Give it posture, voice, and one signature behaviour.
Borrow only that behaviour for this situation. You do not need to become the character.

win: ✓ One useful move borrowed. The character can stay fictional.
supports: Exhale after “Borrow One Move”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Give Posture” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Create Figure → Give Posture → Borrow One Move
safety:
PAUSE
Keep the avatar clearly imaginary and values-consistent.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BUILD THE MINIATURE FIRST
goal: A life change can be tested before full commitment.

steps.action: Create a low-risk scaled version: one-day routine, sample client, temporary location, trial budget, mock conversation.
State what the prototype must reveal and the maximum cost.
Test Miniature it, collect feedback, and redesign before expansion.

win: ✓ I tested the miniature before asking the full-size life change to work.
supports: Exhale after “Test Miniature”; watch the thought.
I can use “State Prototype” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Create Low → State Prototype → Test Miniature
safety:
PAUSE
Check that the prototype is ethically and practically reversible.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
goal: Choices change value while you wait.

steps.action: Notice every option as improving, stable, decaying, or expiring with delay.
Add the date or condition where its arrow changes.
Sequence decisions around genuine expiry rather than anxiety’s false deadlines.

win: ✓ I put time arrows on the options and found the real deadline.
supports: Exhale after “Follow Time Arrows”; watch the thought.
I can use “Add Condition” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Option → Add Condition → Follow Time Arrows
safety:
PAUSE
Verify deadlines rather than assuming urgency.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
goal: Missing information must earn its collection cost.

steps.action: For every desired data point, picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.

win: ✓ Asked what the missing fact could actually change before paying to collect it.
supports: Gently exhale after “Test Relevance”; orient to now.
I can use “Stop Collecting” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Point Positive → Stop Collecting → Test Relevance
safety:
PAUSE
Keep legally, clinically, or ethically required information even when choice impact seems small.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.

steps.action: Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

win: ✓ I let two options enter each round until one earned the next move.
supports: Exhale after “Crown Next”; release the score.
I can use “Pick Criterion” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next
safety:
PAUSE
For high-stakes choices, use the winner only as the next research step and include qualified advice and all safety criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
goal: Sunk cost is history, not future value.

steps.action: Hide what has already been spent.
Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.

win: ✓ The past investment stayed in history and lost its vote on the future.
supports: Exhale after “Remove Sunk Vote”; slow the clock.
I can use “Compare Options” without rushing.
formula_flow: Hide Already → Compare Options → Remove Sunk Vote
safety:
PAUSE
Account for contractual or reputational consequences that genuinely persist.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMAGINE THE FAILURE HEADLINE EARLY
goal: Imagine the plan failed so hidden pathways must speak.

steps.action: Project yourself after failure and name the three most plausible causes—not exotic disasters.
For each, add one prevention, detection sign, or recovery step.
Update the plan before commitment.

win: ✓ The bar came down to a level action can actually reach.
supports: Exhale after “Update Commitment”; release the score.
I can use “Add Prevention” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Project → Add Prevention → Update Commitment
safety:
PAUSE
Do not let pre-mortem become unlimited worst-case story generation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PROTECT THE VALID CHOICE
goal: Endless reopening can destroy good decisions after they are made.

steps.action: Establish the evidence threshold that would justify reconsideration.
Store the rationale and first review date.
When discomfort appears without qualifying evidence, name it post-decision noise and continue implementation.

win: ✓ Post-decision noise lost the power to reopen the choice.
supports: Exhale after “Name Post”; release the score.
I can use “Date Store” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Define → Date Store → Name Post
safety:
PAUSE
Reopen immediately for ethical, legal, health, or safety changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BREAK THE EXPECTED SEQUENCE
goal: Life scripts stay automatic until the next scene is questioned.

steps.action: Picture the culturally expected next step.
Name who benefits, what value it serves, and what it costs you.
Generate one respectful alternative sequence.
Test a small part without declaring war on the whole culture.

win: ✓ One alternate scene became possible without turning culture into the enemy.
supports: Exhale after “Test Small”; keep both sides.
I can use “Name Benefits” before concluding.
formula_flow: Picture Culturally → Name Benefits → Generate → Test Small
safety:
PAUSE
Consider relationship and safety consequences, especially in restrictive environments.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: HIDE THE CROWD’S ANSWER
goal: Check fit before popularity enters the room.

steps.action: Before seeing ratings, likes, rankings, or group preference, assess quality using your own criteria.
Hold the judgement and reasons.
Reveal social proof afterward and change your view only if the crowd supplies new evidence, not mere numbers.

win: ✓ Made the choice before the crowd’s answer entered the room.
supports: Exhale after “View Crowd”; watch the thought.
I can use “Hold Judgement” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Group Preference → Hold Judgement → View Crowd
safety:
PAUSE
Use expert consensus appropriately where specialised knowledge matters.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

steps.action: Say the belief silently.
Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
Picture one real case where it fits.
Picture one real case where it does not fit.
Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

win: ✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.
supports: Exhale after “Shrink the Rule”; release extra blame.
What changed: “Name The Belief” → “Shrink the Rule”?
I can use “Imagine Four Limits” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink the Rule
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use belief boundaries to minimise abuse, discrimination, medical facts, legal duties, or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
